question: Where should My secrets live?
why: It decides whether your secrets reach your other devices without an access key, and whether the sgit command and the web Vault can read them.
options: A vault like any other: on this device first, on the server once there is an access key (proposed)
iCloud Keychain only: syncs for free, but cannot be shared or read outside the app

question: May the app keep vault keys in iCloud Keychain, so that all your devices open the same vaults with no setup?
why: This is what makes sync between your iPhone, iPad and Mac need no steps. It also makes your Apple account a way back into your vaults.
options: Yes, on by default, with a switch to keep them on one device (proposed)
Off by default, a switch to turn it on
Never

question: How should a teammate who was sent a vault get the right to add to it? (issue 110)
why: Today they need an access key for the server as well as the vault key, and nothing gives them one.
options: The access key arrives as the first sealed secret when we swap cards (the people session's proposal)
It travels with the vault invitation
A server change: the vault key is enough
Something else

question: Where should the photo of a person you met be kept?
why: A photo makes the trust map human. In the card it would travel to everyone that person meets, and a card must stay small enough for one QR code.
options: On my device only (proposed)
In their card, sent with it
Both: mine on my device, theirs if they add one

question: Shall I prepare AutoFill, so the app fills passwords and passkeys in Safari and other apps?
why: It is what makes a password manager a daily habit. It needs you to switch on the AutoFill Credential Provider capability and an App Group for ai.sgit.vaults.app in the Apple developer portal.
options: Yes, tell me exactly what to switch on
Later

question: If someone loses every device, how should they get back in?
why: There is no company to reset a password. Recovery is where most password managers are weakest.
options: Three of five people I trust each hold a sealed part (proposed, later)
A printed recovery sheet
Both
iCloud Keychain is enough for now

question: Before someone can be put in a shared vault, who must have confirmed them?
why: It decides how strict the team is. A key that came from a confirmed card cannot be swapped by a server.
options: The person making the vault must have confirmed each member (proposed)
Everyone must have confirmed everyone
Anyone in the team is enough

question: Should the app show who is vouched for by you (sha256:db7f79fdd87e030a), as pki.sgit.ai does?
why: A brief from another session asked for it. The design here has every team trust independently, with no root.
options: No root: every team is its own (proposed)
Show 'vouched by Dinis' as extra information
Yes, pin it

question: Should each device send its activity record on its own when the app opens? (issue 117)
why: Today it is a button on each device, so the picture across your three devices depends on remembering to press it.
options: Yes, with a switch, off by default
Yes, on by default in test builds
No, keep the button
